title: Running networks fast and cheaply
hook: Big GPU server, compression, distillation, edge devices, batching.
inPlainWords: Training gets the attention, but most of the cost and delay comes from running the model millions of times.

useCase.title: Inspect every parcel photo on the packing line in 50 milliseconds
useCase.story: 1,200 parcels an hour pass a camera. The line cannot wait for slow answers, and the warehouse has an unreliable internet connection.

approaches.name: Big GPU server
approaches.what: A powerful server runs the full model.
approaches.greatWhen: Heavy models shared by many users.
approaches.avoidWhen: It adds a network trip and costs a lot when idle.
approaches.example: A cloud GPU serving a large model.

approaches.name: Compression (quantization)
approaches.what: Store the network's numbers with less precision so it runs faster and smaller.
approaches.greatWhen: Most deployments. The quality loss is usually small.
approaches.avoidWhen: Tasks that need very fine numeric precision.
approaches.example: A model half the size, nearly as accurate.

approaches.name: Distillation
approaches.what: A small model copies a big one.
approaches.example: A small inspector model trained from a big one's answers.

approaches.name: Edge device
approaches.what: Run the model on a small computer beside the camera.
approaches.greatWhen: Low delay, offline use, and privacy.
approaches.example: A compact device at the packing line.

approaches.name: Batching
approaches.example: Nightly analysis of the day's photos.

approaches.name: Cheap first check
approaches.what: Run a tiny check first and call the big model only for unclear cases.
approaches.example: Obviously fine boxes skip the big model.

challenge.question: The line needs answers in 50 milliseconds, and the internet is unreliable. What fits best?

options.text: Send photos to a distant big GPU service
options.why: Network delay and outages would stall the line.

options.text: Compress or distill a model, run it at the edge, and add a cheap first check
options.why: It is fast, works offline, and only calls a bigger model for unclear cases.
Defective boxes would already be shipped.

options.text: A GPU server in the warehouse
options.why: Fast enough, but costly and more to maintain than a small edge device.

bestCase.title: Right-size the model for where and how it runs
bestCase.example: A distilled, compressed model runs on a small device beside the camera, answering in 20 milliseconds with no internet needed. Unclear photos go to a bigger model in the back office.

worstCase.title: The biggest model, far away
worstCase.example: Photos travel to a distant server and come back in 400 milliseconds when the internet is busy, so the line stalls. The monthly GPU bill is high, and the servers sit idle at night.

steps.label: Cheap first check
steps.goes: A tiny model clears obviously fine boxes.

steps.label: Compact model on the device
steps.goes: A compressed model judges the rest in 20 milliseconds.
steps.goesWrong: The photo is sent to a distant server to be judged by the largest model.

steps.goes: Unclear cases go to a bigger model.

steps.label: Log for retraining
steps.goes: Hard cases are saved to improve the model.

takeaway: Where a model runs decides its cost and speed. Shrink it, move it close, and only call the big one when needed.
